problem:
The entry ${a}_{12}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ k & -1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

equals $-\frac{1}{2}.$ Find the value of $k.$

$k=${{field-1}}
worked_solution:
First, we need to find the determinant of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ k & -1 & 2\end{aligned}|=1|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|-2|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ k & 2\end{aligned}|+(-1)|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ k & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\,(1\cdot 2-1\cdot (-1))-2\,(0\cdot 2-1\cdot k)+(-1)\,(0\cdot (-1)-1\cdot k) \\  & =(2+1)-2\,(-k)+(-1)\,(-k) \\  & =3+2k+k \\  & =3k+3.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{12}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need ${c}_{12}^{t}={c}_{21}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{21} & =(-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(2\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot (-1)) \\  & =-(4-1) \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{12}^{′} & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{12}^{t} \\  & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{21} \\  & =\frac{1}{3k+3}\cdot (-3) \\  & =\frac{-3}{3k+3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we are told that ${a}_{12}^{′}=-\frac{1}{2}$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-3}{3k+3} & =-\frac{1}{2} \\ -3k-3 & =-6 \\ -3k & =-6+3 \\ k & =\frac{-3}{-3} \\ k & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
